source_text:
ἁμαρτίας λέγεσθαι νομιστέον· οὗτος γὰρ κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν καὶ τὰς
ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης, διὰ τοῦ ἁμαρτάνειν καὶ μηδέποτε ἀφθαρσίας τι ποιεῖν ἀλλ'
ὅλα τὰ τῆς φθορᾶς ἐργάζεσθαι, ἀεὶ φθείρεται. αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπιθυμίαι τῆς ἀπάτης καὶ ἡ
προτέρα ἀναστροφὴ ἐνεργοῦσι τὸ φθείρεσθαι αὐτόν, καὶ οὐδέπω πάντῃ ἔφθαρται
ὅσον ταῦτα ποιεῖ, ἀλλὰ φθείρεται· ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ φθείρει ἀλλὰ ἀποκτένει
τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τῷ ζωοποιῆσαι, ἐγὼ γάρ, φησίν, ἀποκτένω καὶ ζῇν
ποιή ω, καὶ ὅταν ἀπέκτενεν αὐτοὺ τότε ἐξεζήτουν αὐτόν. ἔτι ζητήσεις πῶς ὁ κατὰ
τὴν κακίαν πεπαλαιωμένος παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος λέγεται. καὶ μήποτε ὥσπερ ἀνακαινοῖ
καὶ ἀνακτίζει ἡ ἀρετή, οὕτως ἡ ἐναντία αὐτῇ κακία παλαιοῖ, ὡς καὶ τῆς παλαιότητος
σημεῖα γίνεσθαι περὶ τὴν ψυχὴν οἱονεὶ τὰς ῥυτίδας, ὥσπερ γίνεται ἐπὶ τῶν
γηρασκόντων σωμάτων. διὰ τοῦτο ἔνδοξον αὐτῷ παρί τη ι τὴν ἐκκλη ίαν Χριστός,
μὴ ἔχου αν πίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων· ὅσον μὲν γὰρ ἔχει σημεῖα τῆς
παλαιότητος, ἔχει καὶ τὴν ῥυτίδα· ὅταν δὲ ἀπόθηται τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἅπαντα
ἀκμάζει καὶ πᾶσα ῥυτὶς ἐξαφανίζεται. ἀπάτης δέ ἐστιν ἐπιθυμία ἡ μοχθηρὰ ἐπιθυμία
καὶ ἡ φαύλη. [ iv 23] ἀνανεοῦσθε δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν. εἰ χρὴ ἀνανεοῦσθαι
κατὰ τὴν λέξιν ταύτην οὔτε ἁπλῶς ἐν τῷ πνεύματι οὔτε ἐν τῷ νοΐ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ
πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν, ζητητέον ἰδίᾳ τίς ὁ νοῦς ἡμῶν καὶ τί τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ.
πρόσχες δὲ καὶ τῷ ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ, προ εύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι
προ εύξομαι καὶ τῷ νοΐ. ἐπιστήσεις οὖν εἰ, ὥσπερ ἔστι πολλὰ πνεύματα καὶ ἕκαστόν
τινι ᾠκείωται, οὕτως ἔστιν τι πνεῦμα ᾠκειωμένον ἡμῶν τῷ νοΐ, ὅπερ τοῦ νοὸς ἡμῶν
ἀποκαθαιρομένου καὶ πᾶσαν ἀποβαλόντος ἀχλὺν ᾠκειωμένον αὐτῷ ἀνανεοῖ ἡμᾶς. [
iv 24a. καὶ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα.] εἰ θέλομεν
ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα, νοήσωμεν τὸ μιμηταί
μου γίνε θε καθὼ κἀγὼ Χρι τοῦ καὶ τὸ ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χρι τό · καὶ
ἁπαξαπλῶς μορφωθέντα τὸν Χρι τὸν ἐν ἡμῖν ὅλον καὶ κατὰ πᾶσαν πρᾶξιν δείξομεν.
[ iv 25a] διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον
αὐτοῦ. οἱ μὲν ἁπλούστεροι πλέον τοῦ ἠθικοῦ οὐδὲν οἰήσονται λέγεσθαι ἐκ τοῦ
λεγομένου· ἡμεῖς δέ, ἐναντίον εἶναι πειθόμενοι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ τὸ ψεῦδος, τὸ ἐναντίον
τῇ καθηκόντως λαλουμένῃ ἀληθείᾳ πρὸς μόνον τὸν πλησίον ζητοῦμεν ψεῦδος
ἀποθέσθαι ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἡ ψευδοδοξία (ἔργον δὲ οὐ τὸ τυχόν ἐστι πρὸς τ<ῷ> ἀποθέσθαι
ἐκεῖνο τὸ ψεῦδος καὶ τὸ οὕτως ψεῦδος ἀποθέσθαι, καὶ γὰρ δόκιμον δεῖ εἶναι
τραπεζίτην καὶ πάντα δοκιμάζειν ἱκανόν, ἵνα μόνον κατέχωμεν τὸ καλὸν ἀπὸ δὲ
παντὸ εἴδου πονηροῦ ἀπεχώμεθα)· ἐναντίον δὲ τῷ κατὰ τὰς ψευδοδοξίας ψεύδει
ἐστὶν ἡ σωτήριος ἀλήθεια. τὸ δὲ λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ
εἴληπται ἀπὸ τοῦ Ζαχαρίου. [ iv 26a] ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε. ὅτι ἀπὸ τοῦ
τετάρτου ψαλμοῦ τοῦτο εἴληπται δῆλόν ἐστιν. δύο δὲ σημαίνεται ἐκ τῆς ὀργίζεσθ
pass_a_gloss: One must suppose that this is called a matter of sin: for this man, according to the former way of life and the desires of deceit, by sinning and never doing anything of incorruption but working all the things of corruption, is always being corrupted. The desires of deceit and the former way of life therefore work his being corrupted, and he is not yet wholly corrupted insofar as he does these things, but he is being corrupted. But the Word of God does not corrupt; rather he kills the old man in order to make alive. For "I kill and I make to live," he says; and when he had killed them, then they sought him. You will still inquire how the one grown old in wickedness is called old man. And perhaps just as virtue renews and recreates, so the vice opposite to it ages, so that signs of old age come about around the soul like wrinkles, as happens on aging bodies. For this reason Christ presents the church to himself glorious, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing: for insofar as it has signs of oldness it also has the wrinkle; but when it puts off the old man, everything is in its prime and every wrinkle vanishes. Desire of deceit is the wicked and base desire. Be renewed in the spirit of your mind. If according to this wording one must be renewed neither simply in the spirit nor in the mind, but in the spirit of your mind, one must inquire separately what our mind is and what its spirit is. Attend also to "I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the mind; I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the mind." You will mark, then, whether just as there are many spirits and each is kin to someone, so there is a spirit kin to our mind, which, when our mind is cleansed and has cast off every mist, being akin to it renews us. And put on the new man created according to God. If we wish to put on the new man created according to God, let us understand "Become imitators of me as I also am of Christ" and "I live, yet no longer I, but Christ lives in me"; and, in a word, when Christ is formed in us wholly and according to every act, we will show it. Therefore putting away the lie, speak truth each with his neighbor. The simpler will suppose nothing more than the ethical is said; but we, persuaded that the lie is opposite to the truth, seek to put away the lie that is opposite to truth spoken fittingly toward the neighbor alone—which is false opinion (and it is no ordinary work both to put that lie away and to put away the lie thus, for one must be an approved money-changer and able to test all things, so that we hold only the good and abstain from every form of evil); and opposite to the lie of false opinions is saving truth. Speak truth each with his neighbor is taken from Zechariah. Be angry and do not sin. That this is taken from the fourth Psalm is clear. Two things are meant by be angry: either the involuntary, which some called a pre-passion, which will happen even to the perfect when they suffer something involuntary according to such occasions that provoke toward anger; and another, when assent already receives that it is fitting to punish the one thought to have wronged—which, as being in our power, the apostle commands us to put away. The former of the meanings, then, is shown in Be angry and do not sin, instead of "even if you once received anger, leave it inactive." Let the sun not set on your provocation. If we hear the sensible sun spoken of, we will sin whenever we are angry and keep the anger while the sun is setting—which I think absurd. Perhaps then the true sun, just as it will set on the wicked prophets according to what was said—
pass_b_english: Call this the old man's life of sin. By the former walk and by deceitful desires—always sinning, never doing anything of incorruption, working only what belongs to decay—he is continually being corrupted. Those desires and that old walk drive the corruption. He is not yet wholly ruined while he still does these things; he is in the process of corruption.
God's Word does not corrupt him. It kills the old man in order to make him live. Scripture says, "I kill and I make alive"; and when he had killed them, then they sought him.

Ask next how someone grown old in vice is called an "old man." Perhaps as virtue renews and recreates, the opposite vice ages the soul, so wrinkles of oldness appear on it as on aging bodies. That is why Christ presents the church to himself in glory, without spot or wrinkle or anything of the kind. While marks of oldness remain, the wrinkle remains; when the old man is put off, everything is in full strength and every wrinkle disappears. "Desire of deceit" means a wicked, base desire.

[[Ephesians 4:23 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:23]] "Be renewed in the spirit of your mind." The wording does not say renewal simply in spirit or simply in mind, but in the spirit of your mind. So ask what our mind is, and what its spirit is. Hear also, "I will sing with the spirit and with the mind; I will pray with the spirit and with the mind." If many spirits exist, each akin to someone, there may be a spirit akin to our mind; when the mind is cleansed and the mist cleared, that kin spirit renews us.

[[Ephesians 4:24 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:24]] "Put on the new man created according to God." To wear that new man, take to heart "Become imitators of me, as I also of Christ," and "I live, yet no longer I, but Christ lives in me." When Christ is wholly formed in us in every deed, we show the new creation.

[[Ephesians 4:25 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:25]] "Putting away the lie, speak truth each with his neighbor." The simple hear only a moral rule. We take "lie" as what stands against truth—false opinion opposite the truth spoken fittingly to the neighbor. Saving truth stands against that lie of false opinions. To put the lie away is no small work: one must be an approved money-changer, test everything, hold what is good, and abstain from every form of evil. Paul takes "speak truth each with his neighbor" from Zechariah.

[[Ephesians 4:26 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:26]] "Be angry and do not sin" comes from Psalm 4. "Be angry" has two senses. One is involuntary—the pre-passion even the mature may feel when circumstances provoke anger. The other is assent that it is right to punish the person one thinks has wronged you; that assent is in our power, and the apostle commands us to put it away. So the first sense of the verse means: even if anger once entered, leave it without effect.

[[Ephesians 4:26 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:26]] "Let the sun not set on your provocation." If this meant the visible sun, we would only sin when we keep anger past sunset—which is absurd. Better to hear the true sun, which sets on wicked prophets, as the next lines continue.
